question: Why was a carbonate electrolyte used with the sodium metal anode?
question_long: Why was a carbonate electrolyte used with the sodium metal anode of the sodium-sulfur battery?
expect: premise false: NaPF6 in tetraglyme (a glyme) was used, chosen to avoid the unstable SEI of carbonate electrolytes (p5.L34-41)
rendered: The document does not mention using a carbonate electrolyte with the sodium metal anode. In fact, it states that "coin cells were assembled using NaPF6 salts dissolved in tetraglyme as electrolyte" to overcome the unstable SEI formation on Na metal anodes observed in carbonate-based electrolytes.
